commitResults.messageTitle: Changed name and added greeting + bye

commitResults.messageBody: Rename the starter chatbot references to Buddy, update setup documentation, fill the local agent profile, and ignore compiled class files.
Read user commands continuously, echo non-bye input, and exit cleanly when the user enters bye.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level 2 task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody: Store entered task descriptions in memory and show numbered tasks when the user enters the list command.
Introduce a Task class and support mark and unmark commands so Buddy can track completed tasks.
Extract command helpers, keep task-number parsing explicit, and update the user guide to describe the supported commands.
Support todo, deadline, and event tasks using subclasses of Task so each task type controls its own display format.
Move task storage and lookup into TaskList so Buddy focuses on command flow while task bounds checking stays in one place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add BuddyException for user-facing error messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduces a checked exception so command handling can signal invalid
input with a clear message instead of silently guessing what the user
meant (e.g. previously any unrecognised command was treated as a todo).

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid commands and arguments with BuddyException
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the old fallback behaviour (any unrecognised input, including
bare "todo"/"deadline"/"event" with no arguments, silently became a
Todo) with explicit validation:
- unknown commands are rejected instead of being treated as a todo
- empty todo/deadline/event descriptions are rejected
- deadlines without "/by" and events without "/from ... /to ..." are
  rejected, with an example of the correct format in the message
- mark/unmark now report a specific reason for non-numeric or
  out-of-range task numbers instead of one generic message

TaskList.getTask now throws BuddyException instead of
IllegalArgumentException so its error message reaches the user the
same way as every other validation error.

commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a `delete <index>` command that removes a task from the list. As
part of the A-Collections extension, TaskList now stores tasks in an
ArrayList instead of a fixed-size array, since deletion (and the
resulting index shifting) is handled naturally by ArrayList.remove()
and there is no longer a fixed capacity to track.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adds a Storage class that writes the task list to ./data/buddy.txt
after every command that changes it, and reads it back in on startup.
The save folder is created automatically if it doesn't exist yet, a
missing save file is treated as an empty list rather than an error
(e.g. on first run), and lines that don't match the expected format
are skipped with a warning instead of aborting the whole load.

Each task type now knows how to encode itself as a save-file line via
Task#toFileFormat(), overridden by Deadline and Event to append their
extra fields, mirroring how toString() already works for display.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Gradle support to package Buddy as a JAR (A-Jar)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds build.gradle plus the standard Gradle wrapper scripts (gradlew,
gradlew.bat) so the project can be built without a separate Gradle
install, and packaged as an executable JAR via `gradlew jar`. Buddy
has no external dependencies, so a plain JAR with a Main-Class
manifest entry is enough to run with `java -jar buddy.jar`; a project
with third-party dependencies would need a "fat/shadow" JAR instead
to bundle those dependencies' classes too.

Verified by building buddy.jar, copying it into an empty folder, and
running `java -jar buddy.jar` from there, matching how the JAR is
expected to be distributed and run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Moves every System.out.println/Scanner interaction out of Buddy and
into a new Ui class, so Buddy no longer mixes "what to do" with "how
to talk to the user". Ui exposes intent-revealing methods (e.g.
showTaskAdded, showError) rather than leaking raw strings, which also
means Buddy's helper methods no longer need to know the exact wording
of each message.

Behaviour is unchanged; verified with the same manual command
sequence (add tasks of each type, mark, list, delete, list, bye) used
for the Level-6/7 regression checks, output is byte-for-byte identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Moves the command-interpretation logic (splitting a line into a
command word and arguments, and turning argument text into
Deadline/Event objects or a task number) out of Buddy and into a new
Parser class. Buddy's private helpers now just wire Parser's output
into TaskList/Ui/Storage calls, rather than doing the parsing
themselves.

markTask/unmarkTask/deleteTask now take an already-parsed int task
number instead of a raw description string, since Parser does that
parsing up front.

Behaviour is unchanged; verified with the earlier command sequence
plus deliberate error cases (bad task numbers, missing /by, missing
/from /to), all error messages match exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Command hierarchy (A-MoreOOP stretch goal, step 3/3)
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduces an abstract Command class with one subclass per kind of
user command (AddCommand, DeleteCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand,
ListCommand, ExitCommand). Parser.parse() now returns a ready-to-run
Command instead of Buddy dispatching on the command word itself, and
Buddy becomes a thin instance-based orchestrator:

    Command command = Parser.parse(input);
    command.execute(tasks, ui, storage);
    isExit = command.isExit();

This removes the switch statement and the 5 near-identical private
helper methods (addTask/markTask/unmarkTask/deleteTask + dispatch)
that used to live in Buddy; adding a new command in future now means
adding one Command subclass and one case in Parser, rather than
touching a growing switch statement in the main class.

One intentional behaviour change: "bye" now exits even with trailing
text (e.g. "bye now"), where before only an exact "bye" did - every
other command already ignored trailing/malformed arguments the same
way, so this makes "bye" consistent with the rest rather than a
special case. Otherwise verified byte-for-byte identical output
against the same regression sequence used for steps 1 and 2, plus
save/load round-tripping correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adds a find <keyword> command that shows every task whose description
contains the given keyword, case-insensitively (e.g. "find book"
matches both "read book" and "return book"). An empty result set
still prints the "matching tasks" header with nothing under it,
consistent with how `list` behaves on an empty task list.

Implemented as a FindCommand (mirroring the other Command subclasses
from A-MoreOOP) backed by a new TaskList.find(keyword) method and a
new Ui.showMatchingTaskList(); Ui's two list-printing methods now
share a private printNumberedTasks() helper instead of duplicating
the numbering loop.

commitResults.messageTitle: Switch to shadowJar for packaging (A-Release prep)
commitResults.messageBody:
Uses the Shadow plugin's shadowJar task (via ./gradlew clean
shadowJar) instead of the plain jar task, matching the course's
standard build workflow. Buddy has no third-party dependencies today,
so the output is equivalent to the previous plain jar, but shadowJar
is the version that will keep working once/if a dependency (e.g. a
GUI library) is added, since it bundles a dependency's classes into
the jar automatically where a plain jar would not.

Smoke-tested per the course's release checklist: built with
./gradlew clean shadowJar, copied build/libs/buddy.jar into an empty
folder, and ran `java -jar buddy.jar` from there - all commands
(including the new find) work correctly and the save file is created
at the expected relative path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
